Subject: Questions on DPA roles / SCCs for Order Form

Hi Jordan / Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier. Legal asked us to follow up with a couple of specific points before we circulate counters:

1) The Order Form currently lists BrightBridge as Controller and Redwood as Processor; our privacy team wants clarity on two sub-processor categories (analytics & model tuning). Can Redwood confirm whether model tuning is considered a separate processing purpose under the DPA or if it falls under "service improvements"?

2) The SCCs in the DPA reference a "Controller/Processor" split in Exhibit A but there is no transfer-addendum cited for non-EU hosting. We need an explicit transfer-addendum or confirmation of which SCC clause set you intend to rely on for EU→US routing.

3) Evidence: procurement needs a short list of what technical evidence Redwood can provide (SOC2 cert page, data retention window, KMS details) to attach to our intake.

We'd like to avoid heavy redlines on the MSA/order form if possible, but legal flagged the above as blockers for sign-off. Attaching a short-track doc with the compliance asks (see referenced attachment in our system).

Can you advise owners on your side and an ETA to get a redline back? Our renewal window is tight.

Best,
Selena

Hi all — quick legal response and attached redline. Summary:

1) Model tuning/personalization: recommend we keep it scoped under "service improvements" but include an explicit sub-clause in the DPA that states: "Model tuning involving customer-provided data will only be performed with customer consent and subject to agreed purpose-limited processing; Redwood will not reuse such data for broader model training without explicit opt-in." That should satisfy customers like BrightBridge who want clearer language without creating a separate processing purpose.

2) SCCs / transfer-addendum: proposed approach is to adopt the EU Commission's standard SCCs (Controller-Processor, 2021 modules) and include a short transfer-addendum exhibit listing hosting territories and fallback (US-hosting fallback with approved safeguards). I attach Redwood_DPA_redline_20260826.pdf with the exhibit placeholder language.

3) Evidence: draft a one-page evidence summary (SOC2 link, KMS: customer KM integrations supported, retention defaults with optional retention blocks) — Ben, Jordan please confirm the contacts for SOC2/ops.

I've kept the redline targeted (DPA + exhibit); I avoided touching the core MSA liability stacks so procurement can do a quick tie-out. If BrightBridge wants a specific clause for tuning as a standalone purpose, we can add it but that'll require more procurement discussion.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_redline_20260826.pdf
